To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein fold occurrence within and among genomes can be described with Weibull functions, and the Weibull parameters for genomes can be interpreted in the context of reliability theory.

(1) protein fold distribution within or among genomes can be described with the Weibull probability distribution function; (2) Weibull parameters can be used as indicators of genome evolution; and (3) Weibull reliability analysis can be applied to predict the occurrence of protein fold classes in genomes.

the Weibulls distribution describes the occurrence of protein structures among genomes better than the power function, the Weibull parameter β varies between genomes and can reflect the rate of gene duplication in the evolutionary history of organisms, and that reliability analysis can be used to predict the occurrence of protein structure classes among genomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods and models to describe the occurrence of protein fold families within and among genomes.
the analysis of protein sequence-structure relationships and the application of this knowledge to the study of genome structure and evolution.
developing methods for the analysis of large scale genomic sequence data and their applications in structural genomics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein fold distributions within and among genomes can be described with Weibull functions and the reliability parameter β may reflect evolutionary history of organisms.
Weibull reliability theory is applicable in structural genomics and that the Weibul parameter β can be used to estimate rates of duplication of protein folds in evolutionary history.
the Weibulldistribution describes the protein fold distribution within a genome more accurately than the conventional power law function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Weibul distribution can be used to model protein fold distributions in genomes and that the Weibulls reliability parameter β may be used to characterize the evolution of genomes.
Weibull reliability analysis provides a more accurate description of the occurrence of protein structures within genomes and among genomes than the conventional power law function.

protein fold distribution within genomes can be accurately modelled using Weibull functions, and that the Weibul reliability parameters for genomes can be used as a measure of the rate of gene duplication in the evolution of organisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reliability analysis is an important tool for understanding and predicting evolutionary dynamics in protein fold space.
the reliability analysis of genome-wide fold distributions provides a new perspective on protein structure evolution.
the Weibulls function can be used as a general tool for the description of protein fold distributions within and across genomes.
